ai.description: This turtle reaches 40 cm. Its black shell features radiating yellow spots and prominent vertebral keels. The head is black with small yellow spots and a distinctively elongated, narrow snout.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Geoclemys hamiltonii* is uniquely identified by its high-domed, black carapace adorned with distinct, radiating yellow or white spots and streaks across all scutes.
ai.habitat: The Spotted Pond Turtle inhabits deep, slow-moving or stagnant freshwater bodies like marshes and oxbow lakes, characterized by dense aquatic vegetation and muddy beds.
ai.behavior: The Spotted Pond Turtle is primarily crepuscular, often foraging in shallow, murky waters for mollusks and aquatic vegetation during the dawn and dusk hours.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Geoclemys hamiltonii* is oviparous, typically nesting during the monsoon season (July–August). Females lay 1–3 clutches annually, each containing 12–30 eggs.
ai.distributionRemarks: *Geoclemys hamiltonii* occurs across the Indus and Ganges river basins in Pakistan and northern India, ranging from low-lying wetlands up to 300 meters in elevation.
